intro: Arkansas Legislative Audit examines every county and publishes what it finds. This page quotes what the auditors reported about Columbia County, from its latest report — no verdict added in either direction. What the auditors said is the record; what to make of it is yours.
regulatory_basis_note: Read this before reading any Arkansas audit: county and city reports carry a technical 'adverse opinion' on GAAP grounds because Arkansas law has them keep books on a simpler 'regulatory basis.' That phrase appears in every such audit in the state and signals the accounting format — not wrongdoing. A report is 'clean' or not in its findings, deficiencies, and noncompliance sections, which is what this page quotes.

verdicts.quote: Noncompliance with state law and accepted accounting practices was noted in the office of County Judge. Code Ann. § 14-14-1202.
verdicts.detail: A limited review (a “financial and compliance report”), not a full audit: the financial statements in it are unaudited. The letter continues in the report on page 3; parts that concern staff positions are left to the report, since this site doesn’t single out non-elected staff.

limits: From the 2024 report, dated December 8, 2025. Read by machine from the report’s text; the quotes are the auditors’ words. Older reports, and the separate federal (single) audits, aren’t on this page yet.
Arkansas alternates between full audits and limited “financial and compliance” reviews; each line says which this is.

cities.name: Emerson
cities.quote: Noncompliance with state law and accepted accounting practices was noted in the offices of Mayor and Treasurer. Mayor and Treasurer The Mayor was overpaid a total of $3,000 for 2025 and 2024 due to calculation errors that occurred when the Town changed from monthly to weekly payroll processing. As a result, the Mayor was paid more than the appropriated salary, and none of the overpayment has been recouped, as of the report date. Mayor In 2025, Street Fund disbursements exceeded appropriations by $15,218 (35%) in noncompliance with Ark.

cities.name: Magnolia
cities.quote: Mayor and Advertising and Promotion Commission Chairperson The City paid $1,150 to reimburse a private business for the private business' advertising expense using advertising and promotion tax revenue, in non-compliance with Ark. cities.name: Taylor
cities.quote: Noncompliance with state law and accepted accounting practices was noted in the office of Mayor. Mayor For 2023, Street Fund disbursements exceeded budgeted appropriations by $16,743 (48%), in noncompliance with Ark. Code Ann. § 14-58-203.

cities.name: Waldo
cities.quote: During our evaluation, noncompliance with state law and accepted accounting practices was noted in the offices of Mayor and Treasurer. Mayor and Treasurer The City issued salary overpayments of $2,000 to the Mayor in both 2024 and 2023, in noncompliance with Ark. Code Ann. § 14-42-120.
